books.section: Topic 5.9 Government Policies During the Civil War
Unit 5: Toward the Civil War and Reconstruction (1844–1877)

primary_sources: Thirteenth Amendment to the Constitution (ratified December 6, 1865)

stimulus.source_note: Thirteenth Amendment to the Constitution, proposed by Congress January 31, 1865, ratified December 6, 1865. Public domain. Wording verified against the Constitution Annotated text.
stimulus.text:
“Section 1. Neither slavery nor involuntary servitude, except as a punishment for crime whereof the party shall have been duly convicted, shall exist within the United States, or any place subject to their jurisdiction.

Section 2. Congress shall have power to enforce this article by appropriate legislation.”

—Thirteenth Amendment, as ratified December 6, 1865

source: original; stimulus as noted in stimulus.source_note
stem: The amendment bans slavery “within the United States, or any place subject to their jurisdiction.” Compared with the Emancipation Proclamation, its reach is broader because it covers

options.text: only the states that had been in rebellion against the Union.
options.misconception: Background: the amendment covers the whole country, while the proclamation covered only rebel territory.

options.text: every state, including the loyal border states the proclamation left untouched.
only the territories, and not the states themselves.
options.misconception: Background: the amendment covers the United States and every place under its jurisdiction, states included.

options.text: only the District of Columbia, and nowhere else at all.
options.misconception: Background: the amendment covers the whole country, not the District of Columbia alone.

rationales.A: Background: the amendment covers the whole country, while the proclamation covered only rebel territory.
rationales.C: Background: the amendment covers the United States and every place under its jurisdiction, states included.
rationales.D: Background: the amendment covers the whole country, not the District of Columbia alone.
rationales.B: The amendment bans slavery within the United States and every place under its jurisdiction, so it reaches the border states the proclamation left out.
rationales.general:
1. Read the reach of the words: within the United States, or any place under its jurisdiction.
2. That is everywhere, with no list of excepted places.
3. Background: the proclamation named only rebel territory and left the border states out.
4. The amendment fills exactly the gap the proclamation left.
Remember: compare two documents by their reach, and the wider one finishes the job.
